dishes.name: Blue Prawn Salad
dishes.spielFull: Blue prawn salad with Caledonian blue prawns rubbed in a Szechuan-coriander blend and grilled, served over peppery greens with Japanese mizuna, tossed in our carrot ginger dressing. We finish it with crispy gobo chips, which are burdock root, and pickled tri-color cauliflower for crunch and a little tang. Light, refreshing salad with a bit of spice and texture.
dishes.spielShort: Grilled Caledonian blue prawns over peppery greens in carrot ginger dressing, finished with crispy gobo chips and pickled cauliflower. Light, refreshing, with a little spice and crunch.
cookingMethod: Season: Rub prawns with Szechuan-coriander blend
Grill: Grill prawns until just cooked
Dress greens: Toss peppery greens with carrot ginger dressing
Plate: Arrange greens, top with grilled blue prawns
Finish: Top with crispy gobo chips and pickled tri-color cauliflower
buildPlating: Base: Peppery greens (arugula, frisée, mizuna, watercress, butter lettuce) tossed in carrot ginger dressing
Protein: Grilled Caledonian blue prawns on top
Garnish: Crispy gobo chips (burdock root), pickled tri-color cauliflower
dishes.flavorNotes: Caledonian blue prawn: naturally blue shell, slightly sweet with clean ocean note, firm and juicy texture. Carrot ginger dressing: ginger-forward with a light spice and shiso accent. Light, refreshing salad with a bit of spice and texture.
dishes.notes: Greens differentiation: This uses the 'peppery greens blend' (arugula, frisée, mizuna, watercress, butter lettuce). This is different from the 'spring mix style base' used for Field Greens, Sashimi Salad, Grilled Shiitake Salad, Lobster Salad.

dishes.name: Fluke Yuzu Salsa
dishes.spielFull: Fluke sashimi, nine thin slices, dressed in a spiced citrus cucumber salsa with yuzu, lime, Meyer lemon, and a touch of serrano, finished with a light drizzle of olive oil and topped with micro cilantro. It is a very clean, refreshing sashimi plate with just a gentle hint of heat that sits beautifully between courses.
dishes.spielShort: Nine slices of fluke sashimi dressed in a yuzu cucumber serrano salsa, finished with olive oil and micro cilantro. Clean and refreshing with just a gentle hint of heat.
buildPlating: Base: Fluke sashimi (nine thin slices)
Dress: Yuzu cucumber serrano salsa
Finish: Drizzle of olive oil
Garnish: Micro cilantro

ingredientGroups.label: Yuzu Cucumber Serrano Salsa
items: Ama Toza base (rice vinegar, sugar, salt, soy sauce, bonito, cayenne)

dishes.flavorNotes: Spiced citrus profile that is bright and clean. Fresh cilantro and ginger lift. Gentle heat from serrano (accent, not primary). Cucumber provides refreshing texture. Sweet-savory foundation from ama toza. Silky olive oil finish. No onion in this salsa.
dishes.notes: Preparation timing: Add olive oil drizzle just before sending to keep the plate glossy and aromatic. Serrano role: Used as an accent, not a dominant heat element. Onion-free: This salsa intentionally contains no onion.

dishes.name: Kampachi Aji Panka
dishes.spielFull: Kampachi amberjack sashimi, six pieces. The sauce is a blend of Peruvian spicy red anticucho, sweet citrus miso, fresh aji amarillo pepper, and a house vinegar blend. We heat the vinegar blend just enough to draw out the vegetable flavors quickly, then mix all four components together. Sweet and savory with a little spice and a Japanese citrus note. Finished with crispy tofu skin, pickled sushi ginger, kaiware sprouts, diced red onion, and a sprinkle of soy salt.
dishes.spielShort: Kampachi sashimi with red anticucho, yuzu miso, fresh aji amarillo, and house vinegar blend, all mixed together. Finished with crispy yuba, pickled ginger, kaiware, and soy salt. Sweet, savory, a little spice.
buildPlating: Sashimi: Six pieces of kampachi amberjack
Sauce: Red anticucho, yuzu miso, fresh aji amarillo pepper, and house vinegar blend, all mixed together
Garnish: Crispy yuba (tofu skin), pickled sushi ginger, kaiware sprouts, diced red onion, soy salt sprinkle

ingredientGroups.label: House Vinegar Blend (heated to draw out flavor)

allergenNotes: Soy (red anticucho, yuzu miso, soy salt)
Nightshade (aji panka, aji amarillo, red chili flakes)
dishes.flavorNotes: Sweet and savory red anticucho base with warm spice (cumin, oregano, aji panka). Bright citrus from yuzu miso (yuzu, lemon, lime). Fresh aji amarillo adds complexity and gentle heat. House vinegar blend adds tangy depth with garlic and chili notes. Crispy yuba for textural contrast. Pickled ginger for acid and aromatic brightness.
dishes.notes: Vinegar Blend Technique: The house vinegar blend is heated (not boiled) before mixing. This draws out the vegetable flavors in minutes rather than letting it sit 3-4 days to develop. All four sauce components are mixed together as a unified sauce.

dishes.name: Sawara Yuzu Kosho
dishes.spielFull: Six pieces of Spanish mackerel sashimi on fresh arugula, dressed with our house yuzu kosho. It is citrus forward and quite spicy dressing, with a touch of bonito infused sweet vinegar to balance it out. Each piece gets a dot of aji amarillo aioli, a slice of pickled red onion, and we finish with crispy rice cracker pearls to add a light texture. Bright, citrusy, peppery heat from the yuzu kosho with a fresh bite from the arugula. It eats like a light sashimi salad.
dishes.spielShort: Spanish mackerel on arugula with yuzu kosho dressing, citrus forward and pretty spicy. Finished with aji amarillo aioli, pickled onion, crispy rice cracker pearls. Light, fresh, sashimi salad style.
buildPlating: Base: Fresh arugula bed
Protein: Six pieces of sawara on top
Dressing: Yuzu kosho dressing over the arugula and sashimi
Balance Drizzle: Amazu-tosazu blend drizzled on the side of the plate
Accents: Dots of aji amarillo aioli on the plate, pickled red onion on each slice, sprinkle of crispy rice cracker pearls

ingredientGroups.label: Yuzu Kosho Dressing
items: Yuzu kosho paste (yuzu, salt, green chili)

ingredientGroups.label: Pickled Red Onion
items: Pickling liquid is a blend of tosazu and amazu

dishes.flavorNotes: Bright citrus from yuzu kosho dressing and yuzu juice. Peppery heat from yuzu kosho paste. Subtle sweetness from honey. Fresh, peppery bite from arugula. Tangy acid from pickled red onion. Creamy, subtle heat from aji amarillo aioli. Crunch from rice cracker pearls. Amazu-tosazu drizzle adds gentle sweetness and acidity to balance the salty yuzu kosho.
dishes.notes: Wagyu version is identical build, just swap sawara for A5 wagyu. Amazu-Tosazu Drizzle: This is a sushi kitchen blend (different from the kitchen amatoza). It's drizzled on the side of the plate in a small amount because the yuzu kosho dressing is quite salty. The drizzle balances the dish. Eats like a light sashimi salad thanks to the arugula base and balanced dressing.

It is citrus forward and quite spicy dressing, with a touch of bonito infused sweet vinegar to balance it out. Each piece gets a dot of aji amarillo aioli, a slice of pickled red onion, and we finish with crispy rice cracker pearls to add a light texture. Bright, citrusy, peppery heat from the yuzu kosho with a fresh bite from the arugula. It eats like a light sashimi salad.
dishes.spielShort: A5 Wagyu on arugula with yuzu kosho dressing, citrus forward and pretty spicy. Finished with aji amarillo aioli, pickled onion, crispy rice cracker pearls.
buildPlating: Base: Fresh arugula bed
Protein: A5 Wagyu, 2 ounces min on top
Dressing: Yuzu kosho dressing over the arugula and wagyu
Balance Drizzle: Amazu-tosazu blend drizzled on the side of the plate
Accents: Dots of aji amarillo aioli on the plate, pickled red onion on each slice, sprinkle of crispy rice cracker pearls

ingredientGroups.label: Yuzu Kosho Dressing
items: Yuzu kosho paste (yuzu, salt, green chili)

dishes.flavorNotes: Bright citrus from yuzu kosho dressing. Peppery heat from yuzu kosho paste. Fresh, peppery bite from arugula. Amazu-tosazu drizzle adds gentle sweetness and acidity to balance the salty yuzu kosho.
dishes.notes: Same build as Sawara Yuzu Kosho but with A5 wagyu instead of fish.

dishes.name: Tai Relish
dishes.spielFull: Tai snapper sashimi wrapped around a crispy phyllo dough, set in a butter lettuce cup, topped with our house-made sweet Japanese relish of cucumber, zucchini, white onion, and celery, and a thin slice of jalapeño. Finished with a sprinkle of soy salt. Sweet, crisp and a little heat.
dishes.spielShort: Tai snapper wrapped around crispy phyllo in a butter lettuce cup, topped with house-made sweet Japanese relish and jalapeño, finished with soy salt. Bite-size, two piece minimum.
buildPlating: Base: Butter lettuce cup
Center: Tai snapper sashimi wrapped around crispy phyllo dough
Top: House-made sweet Japanese relish
Garnish: Thin slice of jalapeño
Finish: Sprinkle of soy salt
dishes.flavorNotes: Sweet snapper as the protein centerpiece. Crispy phyllo provides textural contrast. House relish is bright and pickled, sweet-tangy from amazu, with mustard seed bite. Ginger oroshi adds warmth and freshness. Jalapeño slice adds a light heat and fresh pop. Soy salt finish brings savory depth. Butter lettuce cup is tender and acts as a holding vessel. Overall: sweet, crisp, and a little heat.
dishes.notes: Minimum order: Two pieces. Format: Bite-size, served by the piece.

dishes.name: Tai Agave
dishes.spielFull: Six pieces of Japanese snapper sashimi in a sweet and spicy agave aji amarillo sauce with lemon and garlic, finished with fresh aji amarillo pepper to add even more heat, shaved celery hearts for a bit of crunch, and a sprinkle of black salt as a finishing touch. It is clean and bright with real heat and is one of the spiciest sashimi plates we serve, so it can be a bit of a challenge if you are sensitive to spice.
dishes.spielShort: Tai Agave is six pieces of Japanese snapper sashimi in a sweet and spicy agave aji amarillo sauce with lemon and garlic, finished with fresh aji amarillo pepper for extra heat, shaved celery hearts for crunch, and a sprinkle of black salt as a finishing touch.
buildPlating: Base: Sweet and spicy agave nectar sauce
Protein: Six pieces of Japanese snapper sashimi
Garnish: Fresh aji amarillo pepper
Garnish: Shaved celery hearts
Finish: Sprinkle of black salt

ingredientGroups.label: Garnishes
items: Fresh aji amarillo pepper (diced or thin sliced)

dishes.flavorNotes: Sweet agave nectar provides the foundation. Aji amarillo brings mild heat and fruity pepper notes. Fresh aji amarillo pepper adds visual pop and fresh bite. Shaved celery hearts contribute a light, crisp texture and subtle green vegetable note. Black salt finishes with mineral depth and visual contrast. Overall: sweet and spicy with bright, fresh accents. One of the spiciest sashimi plates we serve.
dishes.notes: Portion: Six pieces. Dietary advantage: Naturally soy-free and gluten-free.

dishes.name: Toro Yuzu Miso
dishes.spielFull: Toro sashimi, six pieces, lightly seared on the outside and sitting in a citrus sweet yuzu miso. The sauce is made with Japanese citrus and our house sweet den miso. On top of each slice there is just a tiny spoon of our house jalapeño salsa made from our signature jalapeño dressing, chopped red onion, and fresh serrano, then finished with caviar. So you get rich, buttery toro, a sweet savory citrus miso, and just a little bite and heat from the salsa and caviar to balance the richness. It is one of the more premium sashimi plates we offer and the yuzu miso has a deeper, richer sweetness compared with regular miso.
dishes.spielShort: Lightly seared toro sashimi in a citrus sweet yuzu miso, with a touch of house jalapeño salsa and caviar on each slice.
buildPlating: Sauce base: Citrus sweet yuzu miso on plate
Protein: Six pieces of toro sashimi, lightly seared on the outside
Topping: Tiny spoon of house jalapeño salsa on each slice
Finish: Caviar on top of each sashimi

ingredientGroups.label: Protein
items: Toro (fatty tuna), six pieces, lightly seared

ingredientGroups.label: House Jalapeño Salsa (on each slice)
items: Jalapeño dressing (grapeseed oil, rice vinegar, jalapeño, serrano, garlic)

dishes.flavorNotes: Rich, buttery toro with a light sear for warmth and texture. Yuzu miso has a deeper, richer sweetness compared with regular miso. Sweet, savory, and citrus-forward glaze. Jalapeño salsa adds a little bite and heat. Caviar brings brininess to balance the richness. One of the more premium sashimi plates.
dishes.notes: Portion: Six pieces. Sear: Light sear on the outside, raw center. Salsa placement: Tiny spoon on each slice. Caviar placement: On top of each individual sashimi slice. Position: Premium sashimi offering.

dishes.name: Toro Wasabi Salsa
dishes.spielFull: Toro sashimi, six pieces, lightly seared on the outside and set in a ponzu sauce that we make in house with soy sauce, lemon, and rice vinegar. On top of each slice there is a small amount of wasabi salsa made with kizami wasabi and chopped red onion, then finished with micro cilantro. So you get rich, buttery toro with a light sear for warmth and texture, a bright citrus soy ponzu, clean wasabi heat, and a fresh green finish from the micro cilantro. It is a lighter, more citrus forward toro preparation compared with the yuzu miso version.
dishes.spielShort: Lightly seared toro sashimi in house made ponzu with a touch of wasabi salsa and micro cilantro on each slice.
buildPlating: Sauce base: House made ponzu sauce on the plate
Protein: Six pieces of toro sashimi, lightly seared on the outside, raw in the center
Topping: Wasabi salsa on each slice
Finish: Micro cilantro on top of the sashimi

ingredientGroups.label: Protein
items: Toro, fatty tuna sashimi, six pieces, lightly seared

allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce and hydrolyzed vegetable protein in kizami wasabi; soy in ponzu)
dishes.flavorNotes: Rich, fatty toro with a light sear and raw center. Ponzu keeps the plate light, citrusy, and soy-forward. Kizami wasabi salsa adds clean, punchy wasabi heat plus a little bite from red onion. Micro cilantro lifts everything with a fresh green, herbal note. Overall: light, citrus forward, clean and focused, less rich than the yuzu miso toro.
dishes.notes: Portion: Six pieces. Sear: Light sear on the outside, raw center. Salsa placement: Small amount on each slice. Kizami wasabi is a prepared chopped wasabi condiment, real wasabi root finely chopped and marinated in soy sauce and seasonings.

dishes.name: Salmon Sweet Onion
dishes.spielFull: Six pieces of salmon sashimi topped with our Sweet Onion Salsa, the same bright, savory sweet salsa we use for the taco dishes, then finished with a dot of aji amarillo aioli. Clean sashimi style, but with that taco inspired punch.
dishes.spielShort: Salmon sashimi topped with Sweet Onion Salsa and aji amarillo aioli. Bright, savory sweet, sashimi plate.
buildPlating: Plate style: Sashimi plate
Protein: 6 pieces salmon sashimi
Top: Sweet Onion Salsa spooned over the salmon
Finish: Dot of aji amarillo aioli on each piece
allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce in Sweet Onion Salsa)
dishes.flavorNotes: Bright, savory sweet salsa with the same flavor profile as the taco dishes, turned into a sashimi plate.
dishes.notes: This is basically the taco flavor profile turned into a sashimi plate.

dishes.name: Whitefish Arugula
dishes.spielFull: Nine pieces of delicate fluke sashimi set in our signature jalapeño dressing, which is more garlicky and bright than it is spicy, with acidity from rice vinegar. Finished with sliced aged pecorino cheese on each piece and micro arugula for a fresh, peppery bite. It's a really balanced sashimi plate, clean and flavorful.
dishes.spielShort: Nine pieces of fluke sashimi in jalapeño dressing, topped with sliced aged pecorino cheese and finished with micro arugula. Delicate sashimi plate, garlicky and bright with a mild kick.
buildPlating: Plate style: Sashimi plate
Protein: Fluke sashimi, 9 slices
Dressing: Jalapeño dressing
Finish: Sliced aged pecorino cheese on each piece
Top: Micro arugula
dishes.flavorNotes: Clean, delicate white fish. Jalapeño dressing is garlicky and bright, with rice vinegar acidity. Mild heat (more flavor-forward than spicy). Nutty, aged cheese note from pecorino. Fresh peppery bite from micro arugula. Overall: balanced, clean, flavorful.
dishes.notes: Guest-friendly positioning: 'not really spicy, more garlicky and bright.' Optional variation: can be done with salmon sashimi.

dishes.name: Salmon Pastrami Rice Cakes
dishes.spielFull: Smoked salmon sashimi rubbed with our house-made pastrami seasoning, served on a crispy rice cake, then finished with wasabi shiso aioli, crispy capers, and a touch of red onion and cilantro. You get soft salmon against the crunch of the rice cake, peppery warmth from the pastrami spice, and a clean wasabi herb finish.
dishes.spielShort: Smoked salmon pastrami on a crispy rice cake, finished with wasabi shiso aioli and crispy capers, with a little red onion and cilantro.

Protein: Smoked salmon sashimi
Seasoning: Pastrami rub on the salmon
Sauce: Wasabi shiso aioli mixed with cilantro and red onion

dishes.flavorNotes: Soft salmon against the crunch of the rice cake. Peppery warmth from the pastrami spice. Clean wasabi herb finish.
dishes.notes: Minimum order: 2 pieces.

dishes.name: Tai Truffle Special
dishes.spielFull: Six pieces of Japanese red snapper sashimi set in a bonito-infused, sweet-savory truffle yuzu soy. Topped with thinly sliced eryngii mushrooms and shaved black truffles, then finished with micro celery and a touch of white pepper. Aromatic and elegant, with clean citrus, savory depth, and that earthy truffle finish.
dishes.spielShort: Six pieces of tai sashimi in a bonito-infused sweet-savory truffle yuzu soy, topped with eryngii mushrooms and shaved black truffles, finished with micro celery and white pepper.
buildPlating: Plate style: Sashimi plate

Sauce: Truffle oil + Ama Toza + Yuzu Soy
Top: Thinly sliced eryngii mushrooms
Top: Shaved black truffles
Finish: Micro celery, white pepper
dishes.flavorNotes: Aromatic and elegant, with clean citrus, savory depth, and that earthy truffle finish.
dishes.notes: Bonito-infused, sweet-savory truffle yuzu soy sauce.

dishes.name: Tuna Cilantro Salad
dishes.spielFull: Bigeye tuna sashimi, seven pieces, dusted with salt and pepper and lightly seared on the outside, set around crisp peppery greens, arugula, mizuna, watercress, frisée, and butter lettuce, tossed with shaved daikon, finely diced ginger, finely diced serrano, and cilantro in a bright sesame tosazu dressing with fresh-squeezed Meyer lemon juice. Finished with black sesame seeds. Bright citrus, peppery greens, and a clean heat from serrano. Cilantro is a supporting note, not overpowering.
dishes.spielShort: Seven pieces of bigeye tuna, seared and set around peppery greens with daikon, ginger, serrano, and cilantro in sesame tosazu and Meyer lemon, finished with black sesame seeds.
buildPlating: Center: Peppery greens blend (arugula, watercress, frisée, mizuna, butter lettuce) tossed with shaved daikon, finely diced ginger, finely diced serrano, chopped cilantro, sesame tosazu dressing, and Meyer lemon juice
Around: 7 pieces of bigeye tuna (salt and pepper dusted, lightly seared) set around the greens
Garnish: Black sesame seeds

dishes.name: Wild King Salmon Rocoto
dishes.spielFull: Wild king salmon, sashimi grade, rubbed with Sichuan coriander and pan-seared in our house-made shiso rocoto butter with a splash of yuzu and lemon juice, cooked to medium rare. Served over crispy Brussels sprouts that are flash fried and seasoned simply with salt, finished with micro red shiso and Tokyo negi. Rich and savory, definitely on the spicy side, with just enough citrus to cut through and keep the focus on the wild king salmon.
dishes.spielShort: Wild king salmon, Sichuan coriander rubbed and pan-seared in shiso rocoto butter to medium rare, served with crispy Brussels sprouts. Micro red shiso, Tokyo negi.
cookingMethod: Season: Rub salmon with Sichuan coriander blend
Sear: Pan-sear in shiso rocoto butter with yuzu and lemon juice
Cook: To medium rare
Plate: Over crispy Brussels sprouts
Finish: Micro red shiso, Tokyo negi
buildPlating: Base: Crispy Brussels sprouts (flash fried, seasoned with salt only)
Salmon: On top of Brussels sprouts
Pan Sauce: Drizzle the remainder of the shiso rocoto butter with yuzu and lemon juice from the pan over the salmon and Brussels sprouts
Garnish: Micro red shiso, Tokyo negi

shisoRocotoButter.description: House-made compound butter stick (not a sauce)
shisoRocotoButter.note: Yuzu juice and lemon juice are added separately in the pan during cooking, they are NOT part of the butter itself.

ingredients: Fresh rocoto peppers (whole peppers, not paste)
process: Combine rocoto peppers, Fresno peppers, garlic, palm sugar, salt in a container
Let sit 3-4 days (rest period, not fermentation)
Boil to reduce, 30-45 minutes, until it becomes rocoto sriracha
rocotoSriracha.note: Uses fresh rocoto and Fresno peppers (not fire-grilled, that's for Tai Red Pepper sauce).

dishes.flavorNotes: Rich and savory from the compound butter. Definitely on the spicy side from rocoto sriracha. Herbaceous shiso note. Citrus-bright from yuzu and lemon juice added in pan. Crispy, salty Brussels sprouts for texture and balance.
dishes.notes: Sashimi grade salmon cooked to medium rare. Shiso rocoto butter is a house-made compound butter stick.

serverNotes.important: Rocoto and Shiso Serrano are on the menu. Yuzu Soy is off-menu.
guestInteraction: It is sashimi grade salmon and cooked to medium rare, so it will be slightly raw in the middle.
For the King Salmon specifically, you have three spice options to choose from.
Often let the guest react to the options first, that helps narrow down which one to explain in more detail.
serverNotes.wellDoneRequest: Technically it is possible to cook it well done by asking the chef, but usually say we do not do it well done. If they really want well done salmon, guide them to the Salmon Teriyaki instead.

dishes.name: Wild King Salmon Shiso Serrano
dishes.spielFull: Wild king salmon, sashimi grade, salt and pepper rubbed and pan-seared in butter to medium rare. It sits over shimeji and enoki mushrooms tossed in our sesame onion salsa. We finish it with shiso serrano sauce, our jalapeño dressing layered with fresh shiso and serrano, and top it with micro Japanese red shiso. Gentle heat rather than big spice, so it really highlights the flavor of the sashimi-grade wild king salmon.
dishes.spielShort: Wild king salmon, pan-seared in butter to medium rare, over shimeji and enoki mushrooms in sesame onion salsa, finished with shiso serrano jalapeño dressing and micro red shiso.

dishes.name: Wild King Salmon Yuzu Soy
dishes.spielFull: Wild king salmon, sashimi grade, salt and pepper dusted and pan-seared in butter to medium rare. Dressed with our signature citrus yuzu soy and finished with crispy spinach, garlic chips, a touch of sesame seeds, and pink peppercorn for gentle spice and texture. This is one of our classic Nobu signature dishes that used to be on the menu, very simple and clean, all to highlight the flavor of the wild king salmon.

serverNotes.wellDoneRequest: Technically it is possible to cook it well done by asking the chef, but usually say we do not do it well done. If they really want well done salmon, guide them to the Salmon Teriyaki instead.

dishes.name: Short Rib with Hearts of Palm Purée
dishes.spielFull: We slow-cook the short rib for 48 hours, dust it with our 11-spice blend, and finish it on the grill so the spices toast and the edges pick up a gentle char. It goes into the pan with shimeji and our sweet onion soy, and we glaze it until the meat is glossy and seasoned end to end. We plate over a silky hearts of palm purée with caramelized shallots, then finish with pickled asparagus for brightness.
dishes.spielShort: 48-hour sous vide short rib with our house 11-spice rub, grilled for a light char, then glazed in sweet onion soy with shimeji mushrooms. It sits on a silky hearts of palm purée with caramelized shallots, finished with pickled asparagus.
cookingMethod: Sous vide: 48-hour sous vide short rib (no seasoning during sous vide)
Rub: 11-spice dry rub applied after sous vide
Grill: Finish on grill for light sear marks so the spices toast
Pan finish: Glaze in pan with sweet onion soy and shimeji mushrooms until sauce lightly coats and shines
Plate: Set over hearts of palm purée and caramelized shallots
Top: Pickled asparagus and shimeji from the pan
buildPlating: Hearts of palm purée
Caramelized shallots (layered over purée)
Short rib with pan sauce and shimeji
Pickled asparagus on top

ingredientGroups.label: Hearts of Palm Purée
items: Hearts of palm (oven roasted, then blended)

allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce in sweet onion soy)
dishes.flavorNotes: Deep beefy richness from sous vide and grill. Sweet-savory gloss from sweet onion soy (Maui onion, Fuji apple, fresh ginger, garlic, sesame, a splash of sake, mild jalapeño aroma). Earthy mushroom notes from shimeji. Bright pop from pickled asparagus. Silky base from hearts of palm purée with sweet caramelized shallots. 11-spice rub is warm and aromatic, not hot.
dishes.notes: 48-hour sous vide process. 11-spice rub is warm and aromatic, not hot.

dishes.name: King Crab Uni (Uni Rocoto Butter)
dishes.spielFull: We have an Alaskan king crab leg that is fire roasted and glazed with our uni rocoto butter. You really taste the sweet, oceanic uni, and the Peruvian rocoto chili gives a gentle heat while the butter adds richness. On the side there is a chilled king crab meat salad with root vegetables tossed in a spicy fermented miso vinaigrette, so you get a hot, rich king crab leg and a cool, tangy crab salad to balance it out.
dishes.spielShort: Fire-roasted king crab leg with uni rocoto butter, served with a chilled crab and root vegetable salad in a spicy miso vinaigrette.
buildPlating: Crab leg: Whole Alaskan king crab leg, arrives cooked, then fire roasted. Brushed and glazed with uni rocoto butter during roasting. Finished with chopped chives.
Salad: Chilled crab and root vegetable salad. Tossed in a spicy miso (gochujang) vinaigrette. Plated alongside the crab leg.

ingredientGroups.label: Crab Leg & Glaze
items: Alaskan king crab leg (pre-cooked, fire roasted to order)

ingredientGroups.label: Gochujang Vinaigrette
items: Tosazu (soy sauce, rice vinegar, bonito, mirin, sugar)

allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce, yellow anticucho, tosazu, gochujang)
dishes.flavorNotes: Sweet, meaty king crab with light char from the fire roast. Uni rocoto butter is rich, oceanic, and gently spicy with a bit of citrus lift. Spicy miso (gochujang) vinaigrette gives the crab salad a tangy, savory heat. Hot crab and chilled salad create a nice temperature and texture contrast.
dishes.notes: Fire roasted king crab with two components: hot glazed leg and cold crab salad.

dishes.name: King Crab Shiso Serrano
dishes.spielFull: We have an Alaskan king crab leg that is seasoned with black pepper, tossed in clarified butter, and fire roasted. Right before it leaves the kitchen, we spoon over our shiso serrano jalapeño dressing, which is garlicky with good acidity and a mild, clean chili heat from the fresh shiso and serrano. On the side there is a chilled king crab meat salad with enoki mushrooms and sugar snap peas tossed in a sesame onion salsa. So you get sweet, meaty crab with a garlicky, vinegary shiso and chili dressing, and a cool, mild crab salad next to it.
dishes.spielShort: Alaskan king crab leg fire roasted in clarified butter, finished with shiso serrano jalapeño dressing, served with a chilled crab, enoki, and sugar snap pea salad in a sesame onion salsa.
buildPlating: Crab leg: Alaskan king crab leg, seasoned with black pepper. Tossed in clarified butter. Topped with shiso serrano jalapeño dressing right before it leaves the kitchen.
Salad: Chilled crab meat. Enoki mushrooms. Sugar snap peas. All tossed in sesame onion salsa (Nobu salsa).

ingredientGroups.label: Shiso Serrano Dressing
items: Jalapeño dressing (Grapeseed oil, Rice vinegar, Jalapeño, Serrano, Garlic)

allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce in sesame onion salsa)
Sesame (sesame oil in sesame onion salsa)
dishes.flavorNotes: Sweet, meaty crab with light richness from clarified butter. Shiso serrano dressing is garlicky, lightly acidic, and has a mild, clean chili heat. Sesame onion salsa is more about sesame, soy, and onion than citrus; it coats the salad with flavor without feeling heavy. Overall: hot, cold contrast with sweet crab, mild chili heat, and a cool, vegetable-forward crab salad.
dishes.notes: Fire roasted king crab with shiso serrano dressing.

dishes.name: Umami Chicken
dishes.spielFull: We have a bone-in Jidori chicken breast marinated in our vegetable umami blend - kombu seaweed, shiitake mushroom, soy, and aromatics - then grilled until the outside gets nicely blackened so the marinade caramelizes into a smoky umami crust. It's served over roasted vegetables marinated in a light ginger vinegar spice mix to keep them bright and fresh. We top it with a refreshing kohlrabi salsa and finish with hajikami pickled ginger.
dishes.spielShort: Bone in Jidori chicken breast marinated in kombu, shiitake, and soy vegetable umami blend, grilled and blackened, served with roasted vegetables, kohlrabi salsa, and hajikami pickled ginger.
cookingMethod: Marinate chicken in vegetable umami blend
Grill until the outside gets nicely blackened so the marinade caramelizes into a smoky umami crust
Prepare roasted vegetables marinated in light ginger vinegar spice mix
Top with kohlrabi salsa
Finish with hajikami pickled ginger
buildPlating: Protein: Bone-in Jidori chicken breast, marinated and grilled until blackened on the outside and juicy inside
Vegetable base: Cabbage, celery, and carrots pickled in a light ginger vinegar spice marinade, roasted before service
Topping: Kohlrabi salsa spooned over/around the chicken
Finish: Hajikami pickled ginger spear on the plate

ingredientGroups.label: Kohlrabi Salsa
items: Ama toza (rice vinegar, sugar, salt, soy sauce, bonito, cayenne)

allergenNotes: Soy (soy/soy sauce in umami marinade and ama toza)
Allium (garlic, onion, leeks, green onion, chive)
Celery (in both marinade and vegetable side)
dishes.flavorNotes: Deep savory 'umami' from kombu, shiitake, soy, and slow-marinated aromatics. Smoky, blackened grill crust but still juicy inside. Kohlrabi salsa is crisp, lightly spicy, and vinegar-bright with a little soy depth from ama toza. Roasted cabbage, celery, and carrots bring sweet, toasty notes plus a tangy ginger spice from the vinegar dressing. Overall: savory, smoky, and umami-driven with bright, crunchy, acidic elements to keep it light.
dishes.notes: Marinated in kombu seaweed, shiitake mushroom, soy, and aromatics.

dishes.name: Seafood Nabeyaki Udon
dishes.spielFull: We have a seafood nabeyaki udon that's off the menu - a traditional Japanese hot pot with thick white udon noodles, assorted seafood including white fish, salmon, scallop, and shrimp, plus Japanese mushrooms in a savory soy sauce broth infused with bonito and kombu seaweed. We drop in a whole egg to gently poach in the broth, then finish with crispy shrimp tempura on top. It's very comforting and warming.
dishes.spielShort: Seafood nabeyaki udon - traditional Japanese hot pot with thick udon noodles, assorted seafood, Japanese mushrooms, poached egg, finished with shrimp tempura in savory soy sauce broth infused with bonito and kombu seaweed
buildPlating: Hot pot & broth: Build broth directly in the hot pot with dashi (bonito and kombu base), soy sauce, mirin
Noodles: Add thick white udon noodles into the broth
Seafood: Add 2 pieces white fish, 2 pieces salmon, 1 scallop, 1 shrimp
Mushrooms: Add shimeji, maitake, enoki mushrooms
Egg: Drop a whole egg into the hot pot so it gently poaches in the broth
Finish & garnish: Top with 1 crispy shrimp tempura, sliced scallion (negi), mitsuba
Service: Serve directly in the hot pot, clearly warn the guest it is very hot
allergenNotes: Fish (white fish, salmon, bonito in dashi)
Gluten (udon noodles, regular soy sauce, tempura batter)
Egg (whole egg; egg in tempura batter)
dishes.flavorNotes: Very comforting, savory, warming noodle soup that feels like a Japanese winter hot pot in a bowl.
dishes.notes: Hot pot and handle are very hot, always warn the guest. Traditional Japanese hot pot with thick white udon noodles.

dishes.name: King Crab Udon
dishes.spielFull: We have a king crab udon that is off the menu. It is a pan-glazed king crab udon with white onion and bok choy sautéed in butter. Then we add king crab, build a sweet soy garlic dashi sauce in the pan, and toss thick udon noodles through so they are fully coated in the sauce. From there we transfer everything into a preheated hot pot so it arrives sizzling. We finish with scallion and a Japanese seven-hot spice blend, then drop a raw jidori egg yolk on top for you to break and mix through the noodles for a rich, creamy finish.
dishes.spielShort: Pan-glazed king crab udon with bok choy and white onion in a sweet soy garlic dashi butter sauce, served sizzling in a hot pot with Japanese seven-hot spice, scallion, and a raw jidori egg yolk to mix through for a rich, creamy finish.
cookingMethod: Start: Put butter in a pan
Cook vegetables: Add white onion and bok choy to the pan
Add protein: Add king crab after vegetables
Build sauce: Add garlic, soy sauce, mirin, dashi to give it a gentle coat
Add noodles: Add udon to the pan, it becomes more of a stir-fry udon noodle
Prep hot pot: Separately heat up a hot pot until it is as hot as it gets, sizzling
Set hot pot: Set the hot pot on the plate
Transfer: Transfer all of the udon, king crab, white onion, bok choy mix with the garlic soy butter into the hot pot so it sizzles
Finish: Drop a raw jidori egg yolk on top
Garnish: Sprinkle shichimi and scallion
dishes.flavorNotes: Pan-glazed king crab udon with white onion and bok choy sautéed in butter. Sweet soy garlic dashi sauce. Rich, creamy finish from egg yolk. Served sizzling in a hot pot.
dishes.notes: Runner Script: 'Careful, very hot. Please break the egg yolk and mix it through the noodles for a creamy finish.' Garlic sweet soy sauce is unique to this dish, completely different from Short Rib Sauce. Tell the guest to mix everything, especially breaking the egg yolk, so the noodles take on a creamier texture, like a carbonara.

dishes.name: Blue Prawn Salsa Verde
dishes.spielFull: We have Caledonian blue prawns rubbed with our house spice blend, pan seared in butter, then deglazed with sake. We toss them in a yuzu kosho salsa verde - a Japanese citrus pepper salsa that's green, citrusy, spicy, and herb-driven. Served over charred peppery greens dressed with bonito ponzu. Has a good amount of spice.
dishes.spielShort: Szechuan-coriander rubbed Caledonian blue prawn, pan seared in butter, deglazed with sake, then tossed in yuzu kosho salsa verde, over charred peppery greens dressed with bonito ponzu. Bright, savory, with a little heat.
cookingMethod: Season: Rub blue prawns with Szechuan-coriander blend
Sear: Pan sear prawns in butter until just cooked
Deglaze: Add sake to hot pan to dissolve browned bits and build flavor
Toss: Toss prawns in yuzu kosho salsa verde
Char greens: Separately grill peppery greens (arugula, frisée, mizuna, watercress, butter lettuce) with olive oil to get light char
Dress greens: Toss charred greens with tosazu
Plate: Arrange greens, place 3 pieces of blue prawn on top
Finish: Top with micro cilantro

ingredientGroups.label: Protein
items: Caledonian blue prawn (3 pieces per order)

allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce in tosazu, dry miso in rub)
dishes.flavorNotes: Bright citrus-pepper heat from yuzu kosho. Herbal jalapeño-cilantro notes. Light smoke from charred greens. Gentle tang from tosazu. Has a good amount of spice.
dishes.notes: Same Caledonian blue prawn as Blue Prawn Salad. Blue Prawn Spice Rub is specific to blue prawn dishes, different from Fish Rub. Three pieces per order.

dishes.name: Kurodai Black Snapper
dishes.spielFull: Kurodai black snapper rubbed with our Szechuan coriander spice blend and grilled, served with roasted Brussels sprouts tossed in a tomatillo salsa, then finished with micro cilantro and a grilled lemon to squeeze over the top. It is similar to a branzino preparation, but the fish is a little firmer and the rub gives it a gentle Szechuan spice instead of an Mediterranean herbs.
dishes.spielShort: Grilled Kurodai black snapper with Szechuan coriander rub, roasted Brussels sprouts in tomatillo salsa, finished with micro cilantro and a grilled lemon. Similar to branzino but a bit firmer with gentle Szechuan spice.
cookingMethod: Season: Rub fish with Szechuan coriander blend
Grill: Grill Kurodai until just cooked
Prepare sprouts: Roast Brussels sprouts, toss in tomatillo salsa
Plate: Arrange fish with Brussels sprouts
Finish: Top with micro cilantro, serve with grilled lemon wedge to squeeze
allergenNotes: Nightshade (jalapeño in tomatillo salsa, cayenne in rub)
dishes.flavorNotes: Firm, delicate white fish. Earthy, smoky spice from Szechuan coriander rub. Bright, herbaceous tomatillo salsa with a touch of heat. Fresh cilantro accent. Citrus lift from grilled lemon.
dishes.notes: Similar to a branzino preparation, but the fish is a little firmer and the rub gives it a gentle Szechuan spice instead of Mediterranean herbs. Brussels sprouts are roasted, not crispy flash-fried.

dishes.name: Tai Red Pepper
dishes.spielFull: Japanese red snapper fillet rubbed with our Szechuan-coriander spice blend and pan seared in butter. We plate over a fire-roasted red pepper sauce, quite spicy with a nice smoky character, then add sautéed spinach tossed in a bright cherry tomato vinaigrette for a gentle acidity to balance the heat, and set the fish right on top. Firmer white fish with good heat, but well balanced from the vinaigrette and greens.
dishes.spielShort: Japanese red snapper, Szechuan-coriander rubbed and pan seared in butter, plated over a spicy fire-roasted red pepper sauce with sautéed spinach in cherry tomato vinaigrette for a gentle acidity to balance the heat.
cookingMethod: Season: Rub Japanese snapper fillet with Szechuan-coriander blend
Sear: Pan sear in butter until cooked through
Roast peppers: Grill red bell pepper and Fresno pepper until skins are fully blackened
Peel: Remove all blackened skin so only the tender roasted flesh remains
Blend: Purée with garlic, honey, fish sauce, light soy sauce, and rice wine vinegar until smooth
Plate sauce: Spoon roasted red pepper sauce as the base
Add spinach: Top with sautéed spinach tossed in cherry tomato vinaigrette
Finish: Set fish on top
allergenNotes: Fish (snapper, fish sauce in sauce and vinaigrette, bonito in tosazu)
Nightshade (Fresno, bell pepper, serrano, cayenne in rub)
dishes.flavorNotes: Smoky, spicy red pepper sauce with a hint of sweetness to round out the heat. Bright, tangy cherry tomato vinaigrette for contrast. Warm, aromatic Szechuan-coriander spice on the fish. Quite spicy.
dishes.notes: Roasting technique (charring until fully black, then peeling clean) gives the sauce its signature smoky character. Good guest line: 'Smoky red pepper sauce built from fire-roasted peppers.'

dishes.name: New Zealand Snapper
dishes.spielFull: We have a whole New Zealand snapper that is rubbed with our Szechuan coriander fish rub, lightly dusted in potato starch, then flash fried so the skin turns crisp while the flesh stays tender. On the side you get bok choy that is steamed first, then finished on the grill and tossed in a spicy cherry tomato vinaigrette for a bright, tangy contrast. It also comes with a caramelized lemon that is dusted with pink, white, and black peppercorns, marjoram, and a little sugar. When you squeeze that over at the table you get a smoky peppercorn aroma and it really opens up the flavor of the fish.
dishes.spielShort: Whole New Zealand snapper rubbed with Szechuan coriander and flash fried crisp, served with steamed then grilled bok choy in cherry tomato vinaigrette and a peppercorn dusted caramelized lemon to squeeze over.
cookingMethod: Season: Rub whole snapper with Szechuan-coriander blend
Dust: Coat with potato starch
Fry: Flash fry until crisp shell forms, flesh stays tender
Steam bok choy: Steam bok choy until just tender
Grill bok choy: Finish on the grill for a light char
Dress: Toss bok choy in cherry tomato vinaigrette
Prep lemon: Coat lemon with pink, white, and black peppercorns, marjoram, and sugar
Caramelize: Heat until sugar caramelizes
Plate: Plate fish with bok choy alongside, serve caramelized lemon for guest to squeeze
allergenNotes: Fish (snapper, fish sauce in vinaigrette, bonito in tosazu)
dishes.flavorNotes: Crisp, aromatic shell from the Szechuan-coriander rub and flash fry. Tender, flaky white fish inside. Bright, tangy, spicy cherry tomato vinaigrette on the bok choy. Caramelized lemon with warm peppercorn notes to finish.
dishes.notes: Point out the caramelized lemon and tell guests they can squeeze it over the fish to open up the flavor. The fish is technically deep fried, not 'flash fried.' Bok choy is steamed first and then grilled, so it has both tenderness and a bit of char.

dishes.name: NZ Snapper Honey Anticucho
dishes.spielFull: We have a whole New Zealand snapper that's rubbed with smoked paprika, ginger, garlic, and white pepper, deboned and cut into bite-size pieces, then coated in a light tempura batter and deep fried until crisp. We flash-fry Brussels sprouts and Fresno peppers separately, then toss everything together in our house honey anticucho sauce - a Peruvian-style sweet and spicy sauce with red and yellow anticucho, honey, and a touch of mayo for creaminess. It has a good kick that's balanced by the honey. We pile all the crispy pieces back over the fried head, spine, and tail so it still looks like a whole fish when it arrives.
dishes.spielShort: Whole New Zealand snapper rubbed with smoked paprika, tempura fried in bite-size pieces, tossed with Brussels sprouts and Fresno peppers in honey anticucho sauce - sweet, spicy with a good kick, served over the whole fish frame
cookingMethod: Rub whole fish: Season whole New Zealand snapper with smoked paprika, ginger, garlic, and white pepper
Debone and cut: Debone and cut the snapper into bite size pieces, reserving head, spine, and tail for plating
Batter and fry fish: Coat snapper pieces in a light tempura batter and deep fry until very crisp
Fry vegetables: Flash fry Brussels sprouts and Fresno peppers with no batter and no seasoning
Sauce and toss: Toss fish and vegetables together in honey creamy anticucho sauce
Plate on bones: Place the fried head, spine, and tail on the plate, then pile the dressed fish and vegetables back over and around the bones so it reads as a whole fish
Finish: Light smoked paprika finish

ingredientGroups.label: Protein
items: Whole New Zealand snapper (deboned, cut into bite-size pieces, bones reserved for plating)

ingredientGroups.label: Vegetables
items: Brussels sprouts (flash fried, no batter, no seasoning)
Fresno peppers (flash fried, no batter, no seasoning)

allergenNotes: Gluten (tempura batter, soy sauce in yellow anticucho)
Nightshade (smoked paprika, aji panka, aji amarillo, Fresno peppers)
dishes.flavorNotes: Crispy tempura snapper pieces with a light, crunchy shell. Sweet and spicy honey creamy anticucho with a real kick, balanced by honey and mayo. Extra heat and aroma from Fresno pepper. Roasted, nutty notes from flash fried Brussels sprouts. Overall: sauce forward, sweet and spicy, big flavor, very snackable, presented like a whole fish.
dishes.notes: Call out that it is the same whole New Zealand snapper, just in a dressed, crispy version that is more sauce driven. Mention that it is sweet and spicy with a good amount of kick. Already deboned and cut into bite size pieces, even though it is presented over the whole fish frame.

dishes.name: Wagyu Gyoza
dishes.spielFull: We have Nobu-style gyoza dumplings filled with Japanese A5 wagyu and our house-made kimchi. We pan-sear them for a crispy bottom, then steam to lock in all the juices. They're dressed with tosazu - our bonito soy vinegar - mixed with chili oil, and finished with chili flakes, crispy garlic chips, and Tokyo negi. You get rich wagyu, a little kimchi tang, and savory heat from the chili oil.
dishes.spielShort: Nobu gyoza dumplings filled with A5 wagyu and house-made kimchi, pan-seared and steamed, dressed with tosazu chili oil, finished with chili flakes, garlic chips, Tokyo negi
cookingMethod: Fill: A5 wagyu mixed with ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, negi, and katakuriko, plus house-made kimchi folded in
Pan sear: Sear the bottoms in a hot pan until golden and crisp
Steam: Add liquid and cover to steam until cooked through, this captures the juices inside
Dress: Drizzle with tosazu chili oil
Garnish: Top with chili flakes, crispy garlic chips, and Tokyo negi

ingredientGroups.label: Wagyu Filling
items: Japanese A5 wagyu mixed with ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, negi, katakuriko

allergenNotes: Soy (soy sauce in wagyu filling, tosazu)
Fish (fish sauce in kimchi, bonito in tosazu)
Sesame (sesame oil in tosazu chili oil)
dishes.flavorNotes: Rich, umami-forward wagyu. Tangy, spicy kimchi tang. Savory heat from tosazu chili oil. Crispy, aromatic garlic chips for texture contrast. Fresh negi brightness.
dishes.notes: Two-step cook is essential: pan sear then steam to capture the juices inside the gyoza rather than drying them out. House-made kimchi is fermented 3 days. Both wagyu and kimchi are inside each dumpling for a rich, complex filling. Wrapper is wonton shell, same as the tacos.

dishes.name: Okinawa Japanese Purple Sweet Potato
dishes.spielFull: We have a Japanese purple sweet potato that we roast over oak wood chips so it picks up a delicate smoky aroma, then finish it in the broiler. After broiling, we toss it in clarified butter so the outside gets a light glaze and finish it with sea salt. It is naturally sweet and earthy with a gentle touch of smoke and a rich butter finish.
dishes.spielShort: Japanese purple sweet potato roasted over oak, lightly glazed in clarified butter and finished with sea salt. Naturally sweet, earthy, and gently smoky.
cookingMethod: Smoke: Roast Japanese purple sweet potato over oak wood chips to infuse smoke
Salamander Finish: Transfer to the salamander broiler to finish
Butter: Toss potatoes with clarified butter so each piece is glossy
Salt: Finish with sea salt (salt crystals remain visible)
Serve: Plate hot, directly from salamander, so butter glazes and aroma releases right as it hits the table
dishes.flavorNotes: Naturally sweet and earthy from the Okinawan potato. Subtle, clean smoky aroma from oak wood. Rich finish from clarified butter. Bright salinity and crunch from finishing salt.
dishes.notes: Serve hot for best texture and aroma. Pure potato, no sugar, no dressing, no caramelization. A 'salamander' is a high-heat overhead broiler (grills from above).

dishes.name: Karaage Chicken
dishes.spielFull: Nobu-style Japanese fried chicken, half jidori chicken brined for 24 hours in spiced vodka with chili, garlic, and ginger, then air-dried for 24 hours before we coat it in our house-made harissa tempura batter and fry it extra crisp. Served with our house aji limo hot sauce, think of it like our Peruvian tabasco, vinegar-forward with serious heat. Six pieces, crisp outside, juicy inside. Only available on the weekend.
dishes.spielShort: Half jidori chicken, 24-hour spiced vodka brine, air-dried 24 hours, coated in house-made harissa tempura batter, fried extra crisp. Served with house aji limo hot sauce, our Peruvian tabasco. Weekend special.
cookingMethod: Wet brine 24 hours in spiced vodka brine, vodka helps spices penetrate deeper and keeps the meat moist
Rest 24 hours, brings the chicken to just the right moisture level to properly coat in the batter
Coat in house-made harissa tempura batter (made specifically for this dish)
Fry until extra crisp and golden
Serve with house aji limo hot sauce

ingredientGroups.label: Protein
items: Half jidori chicken, 6 pieces (breast x3, thigh x1, leg x1, wing x1)

ingredientGroups.label: House Aji Limo Hot Sauce (our house-made tabasco)

dishes.flavorNotes: Extra crisp, golden exterior from the harissa tempura batter. Moist, tender, juicy meat inside from the spiced vodka brine. Warm, aromatic spice from harissa (chili, cumin, coriander, caraway). Layers of heat from marash, chile de arbol, cayenne. House aji limo hot sauce adds bright, vinegar-forward Peruvian heat.
dishes.notes: Weekend special only, 48-hour process requires advance prep. Half jidori chicken, 6 pieces: More volume than typical dishes. Spiced vodka brine: Vodka carries the spice flavors deeper into the meat and keeps it moist and tender through frying.

dishes.name: Scallop Bibimbap
dishes.spielFull: Scallop bibimbap is a rice dish served in a hot pot with seven grain rice. We grill the scallops and toss them in our creamy sesame chili sauce, then set them over rice in a hot pot with a new style oil blend of sesame and olive oil so the bottom turns crisp. We lightly torch the scallops in the hot pot for a gentle smoky note, then finish with our house made toasted seaweed rice seasoning, smelt egg, and chive. It is creamy and sesame forward with mild spice and a subtle smokiness, and it is one of our rare rice dishes that does not come from the sushi kitchen.
dishes.spielShort: Grilled scallops with creamy sesame chili sauce over 7 grain rice in a hot pot, lightly torched, then finished with toasted seaweed rice seasoning, smelt egg, and chive.
cookingMethod: Prepare rice: 2 cups white rice + 1 cup seven-grain rice cooked in rice cooker
Heat oil in hot pot: Add new-style oil blend (sesame and olive oil) to hot pot
Build base: Add rice to hot pot so bottom crisps
Grill scallops: 3 pieces scallops, each cut into 4 for a total of 12 bites
Toss in sauce: Grilled scallops tossed in creamy sesame chili sauce
Plate: Place scallops over rice in hot pot
Torch: Lightly torch the scallops in the pot to bring out the scallop flavor
Finish: Top with house-made toasted seaweed rice seasoning, masago, and chive

ingredientGroups.label: Protein
items: Scallops (3 pieces, each cut into 4 bites = 12 total)

allergenNotes: Sesame (sesame oil, house rice seasoning, creamy sauce)
Eggs (mayonnaise in creamy sauce, masago fish egg)
Nightshade (aji panka, rocoto peppers, red jalapeño in rocoto sriracha)
dishes.flavorNotes: Creamy and sesame forward with mild spice and a subtle smokiness. One of our rare rice dishes that does not come from the sushi kitchen.
dishes.notes: Weekend only. Hot pot is extremely hot, advise guest. Tell the guest to mix everything well before eating, breaking up the scallops and lifting the crispy rice from the bottom. Rice production is approximately 8 orders per night.

dishes.name: Mandarin Yuzu Kakigori
dishes.spielFull: Our Nobu-style Japanese kakigori is a citrus-forward shaved ice layered with mandarin and yuzu syrup, served over a scoop of vanilla gelato for a creamy base. Finished with dulce de leche pearls, mandarin crunch, and plain frozen mandarin and lemon segments, then drizzled again with mandarin yuzu syrup. It's bright and refreshing like traditional kakigori, but with more richness and texture from the gelato and crunchy toppings.
dishes.spielShort: Nobu-style kakigori shaved ice layered with mandarin and yuzu syrup over vanilla gelato, topped with dulce de leche pearls, mandarin crunch, and frozen mandarin and lemon segments, finished with a final syrup drizzle.
buildPlating: Base: 1 scoop vanilla gelato (bottom of the bowl)
Topping layer 1: dulce de leche pearls + mandarin crunch + frozen mandarin and lemon segments
Shaved ice: kakigori shaved ice
Syrup layer: mandarin yuzu syrup over the shaved ice
Topping layer 2: repeat the same toppings
Final finish: final drizzle of mandarin yuzu syrup over the top
allergenNotes: Gluten (dulce de leche pearls, mandarin crunch)
dishes.flavorNotes: Bright mandarin + yuzu citrus. Creamy vanilla depth from the gelato. Crunch and texture from pearls and mandarin crunch. Cold citrus pops from frozen mandarin and lemon segments.

dishes.name: Seiko Gani
dishes.spielFull: We have one of our more traditional Japanese dishes called Seiko Gani, a Japanese female snow crab that is prized in winter for its rich, flavorful eggs. We boil the whole crab, chill it, then pick the meat and eggs and present them back in the shell. On one side you have delicate sweet crab meat, on the other rich crab eggs. It is finished with a chilled tosazu jelly, which is a classic Japanese bonito infused sweet soy vinegar jelly. The flavor is sweet, savory, and gently tangy, just enough to highlight the natural flavor of the crab without overpowering it. It is fully cooked and served chilled, with a small shiso flower on top as an accent.
dishes.spielShort: Seasonal Japanese female snow crab, cooked and chilled, served back in the shell with sweet crab meat, rich crab eggs, and a light bonito infused sweet soy vinegar jelly.
cookingMethod: Boil: Boil the whole Seiko Gani (female snow crab)
Chill: Chill the crab completely
Pick: Pick the meat and eggs from the shell
Present: Arrange crab meat on one side, crab eggs on the other, back in the shell
Finish: Add chilled tosazu jelly and shiso flower on top
Serve: Served cold

items: Seiko Gani, Japanese female snow crab (1 pc per order)

dishes.flavorNotes: No extra seasoning on the crab, pure crab flavor. Tosazu jelly: sweet, savory, and gently acidic rather than heavy. Delicate, sweet crab meat on one side. Rich crab eggs on the other side. Fully cooked, served cold.
dishes.notes: Seasonal Japanese winter specialty. Female snow crab is prized for its rich roe and flavorful eggs. NO LONGER AVAILABLE.

dishes.name: Silk & Ember
dishes.spielFull: I wanted to mention one cocktail that is off the menu. It is called Silk and Ember and it drinks like a Nobu Malibu style Japanese holiday Old Fashioned. We start with Armagnac brandy, which is a very elegant, spice driven style of brandy, and stir it with a dry Japanese sake vermouth, a little allspice liqueur, and our Japanese black sugar syrup infused with cinnamon and clove that we make in house. Then we add a couple dashes of cocoa bitters and serve it over a single large Nobu stamped rock, finished with torched rosemary and a fresh cranberry on top.
dishes.spielShort: Nobu-style Japanese holiday Old Fashioned. Armagnac instead of whiskey, sake vermouth, Jamaican allspice liqueur, house-made honey syrup with cinnamon and clove. Torch rosemary and a cranberry on top.
cookingMethod: Pour 2 oz Cardinal du Four Armagnac into stirring tin
Add 0.5 oz Oka Kura Dry Bermutto
Add 0.25 oz St. Elizabeth Allspice Dram
Add 0.25 oz house-made Japanese honey syrup
Add 2 dashes Angostura Cocoa Bitters
Add draft ice & stir (30 seconds)
Strain
Add ice to glass (Nobu-stamped large cube)
Garnish, Rosemary Torch (3-5 seconds until smoking, perch cranberry on rosemary)

dishes.flavorNotes: Rosemary smoke on the nose and rich baking spice, caramel and a hint of chocolate on the palate. All the holiday vibes in a spirit-forward Nobu Malibu holiday cocktail. Armagnac has a richer, spicier character than Cognac, making it perfect for holiday flavors.
dishes.notes: Drinks like a Nobu Malibu style Japanese holiday Old Fashioned. Armagnac instead of whiskey. NO LONGER AVAILABLE, December Cocktail of the Month.

dishes.name: Pumpkin Pie
dishes.spielFull: House-baked pumpkin pie topped with white chocolate vanilla ganache, a smooth, creamy white chocolate vanilla pastry cream, and finished with pine nut pumpkin seed crumble sprinkled over the top. Served with espresso gelato on the side. Warm autumn spice balanced by a rich coffee note from the gelato. It's our seasonal special, available only for a short period.
